claim: Experience-dependent reorganisation of functional maps in the cerebral cortex is well described in the primary sensory cortices.
source: Experience-dependent reorganisation of functional maps in the cerebral cortex is well described in the primary sensory cortices.
evidence: This is a general statement about established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: There is relatively little evidence for cortical reorganisation over the short-term.
source: However, there is relatively little evidence for such cortical reorganisation over the short-term.
evidence: This statement characterizes the state of the literature and identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: A 24 hr gluing manipulation in which the right index and right middle fingers were adjoined with surgical glue was performed.
source: Using human somatosensory cortex as a model, we investigated the effects of a 24 hr gluing manipulation in which the right index and right middle fingers (digits 2 and 3) were adjoined with surgical glue.
evidence: This describes the experimental manipulation performed in the study.

claim: Somatotopic representations were assessed with two 7 tesla fMRI protocols.
source: Somatotopic representations, assessed with two 7 tesla fMRI protocols, revealed rapid off-target reorganisation in the non-manipulated fingers following gluing, with the representation of the ring finger (digit 4) shifted towards the little finger (digit 5) and away from the middle finger (digit 3).
evidence: This describes the methodology used to assess somatotopic representations.

claim: Rapid off-target reorganisation in the non-manipulated fingers occurred following gluing, with the representation of the ring finger (digit 4) shifted towards the little finger (digit 5) and away from the middle finger (digit 3).
source: Somatotopic representations, assessed with two 7 tesla fMRI protocols, revealed rapid off-target reorganisation in the non-manipulated fingers following gluing, with the representation of the ring finger (digit 4) shifted towards the little finger (digit 5) and away from the middle finger (digit 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the fMRI data analysis.

claim: Shifts in cortical representation were evident in two behavioural tasks conducted in an independent cohort, showing reduced sensitivity for discriminating the temporal order of stimuli to the ring and little fingers.
source: These shifts were also evident in two behavioural tasks conducted in an independent cohort, showing reduced sensitivity for discriminating the temporal order of stimuli to the ring and little fingers, and increased substitution errors across this pair on a speeded reaction time task.
evidence: This describes behavioral findings that corroborate the fMRI results.

claim: Increased substitution errors across the ring and little finger pair occurred on a speeded reaction time task.
source: These shifts were also evident in two behavioural tasks conducted in an independent cohort, showing reduced sensitivity for discriminating the temporal order of stimuli to the ring and little fingers, and increased substitution errors across this pair on a speeded reaction time task.
evidence: This describes behavioral findings from the motor confusion task.

claim: Evidence for experience-dependent plasticity in the adult mammalian brain exists across a variety of sensory modalities.
source: Evidence for experience-dependent plasticity in the adult mammalian brain exists across a variety of sensory modalities (Fu and Zuo, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The ordered somatotopy of primary somatosensory cortex (SI) has long served as a model system for studies of cortical reorganisation.
source: The ordered somatotopy of primary somatosensory cortex (SI) has long served as a model system for studies of cortical reorganisation, with a wealth of evidence from both the non-human primate and rodent literature linking both extreme and subtle peripheral changes in somatosensory inputs over months or years to alterations in cortical maps (Buonomano and Merzenich, 1998; Feldman and Brecht, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There is a wealth of evidence from both the non-human primate and rodent literature linking both extreme and subtle peripheral changes in somatosensory inputs over months or years to alterations in cortical maps.
source: The ordered somatotopy of primary somatosensory cortex (SI) has long served as a model system for studies of cortical reorganisation, with a wealth of evidence from both the non-human primate and rodent literature linking both extreme and subtle peripheral changes in somatosensory inputs over months or years to alterations in cortical maps (Buonomano and Merzenich, 1998; Feldman and Brecht, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There has been evidence of experience-dependent remapping in SI in the human brain.
source: In the human brain, there has also been evidence of experience-dependent remapping in SI.
evidence: This statement summarizes existing literature on human SI plasticity.

claim: Considerable emphasis has been placed upon cross-sectional differences in the cortical organisation of SI observed in specialist populations, such as musicians, or patients with sensorimotor dysfunction, such as focal dystonia.
source: Considerable emphasis has been placed upon cross-sectional differences in the cortical organisation of SI observed in specialist populations, such as musicians, or patients with sensorimotor dysfunction, such as focal dystonia (Elbert et al., 1995; Bara-Jimenez et al., 1998; Nelson et al., 2009; Kalisch et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Only limited longitudinal evidence exists that directly demonstrates remapping at the level of human SI, either in response to altered hand usage patterns or more intensive Hebbian co-activation paradigms delivering specific patterns of tactile stimulation to the fingertips.
source: However, only limited longitudinal evidence exists that directly demonstrates remapping at the level of human SI, either in response to altered hand usage patterns (Stavrinou et al., 2007) or more intensive Hebbian co-activation paradigms delivering specific patterns of tactile stimulation to the fingertips (Pleger et al., 2001, 2003; Hodzic et al., 2004; Vidyasagar et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and identifies a gap in the field.

claim: There remains a limited understanding of the speed of SI plasticity and how cortical changes relate to behaviour.
source: There remains a limited understanding of the speed of SI plasticity and how cortical changes relate to behaviour.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: A well-validated paradigm of single-subject fMRI mapping of human SI at 7 tesla was used.
source: Using a well-validated paradigm of single-subject fMRI mapping of human SI at 7 tesla (Sanchez-Panchuelo et al., 2010; Kolasinski et al., 2016), we asked two questions.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study and is supported by citations.

claim: Based on the primate literature, forced co-use of the glued digit pair would result in increased tactile co-activation across the digits, and an increase in their shared cortical representation.
source: Based on the primate literature (Clark et al., 1988; Allard et al., 1991), we hypothesised that forced co-use of the glued digit pair would result in increased tactile co-activation across the digits, and an increase in their shared cortical representation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on previous primate studies, supported by citations.

claim: An alternative hypothesis posited that compensatory behaviour during the 24 hr gluing manipulation would promote changes in the cortical representations of adjacent, but unaffected digits.
source: An alternative hypothesis posited that compensatory behaviour during the 24 hr gluing manipulation would promote changes in the cortical representations of adjacent, but unaffected digits.
evidence: This is an alternative hypothesis proposed by the authors based on reasoning about potential compensatory behaviors.

claim: SI digit somatotopy of the right hand was mapped at 7 tesla after two periods of normal hand use (control 1 and control 2), and after the gluing manipulation.
source: In the fMRI cohort, SI digit somatotopy of the right hand was mapped at 7 tesla (Kolasinski et al., 2016) after two periods of normal hand use (control 1 and control 2), and after the gluing manipulation.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the fMRI study.

claim: fMRI data were acquired during a block design task and phase-encoding task in each session.
source: In each session, fMRI data were acquired during a block design task and phase-encoding task.
evidence: This describes the data acquisition protocol.

claim: A two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on the amount of cortical overlap (F(4,32) = 13.412, p<0.0005, η2:0.626).
source: A two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on the amount of cortical overlap (F(4,32) = 13.412, p<0.0005, η2:0.626) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of fMRI data.

claim: There was a significant reduction in the cortical overlap between D3-D4 in the glued condition compared with both control sessions (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 23.379, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05).
source: This was driven by a significant reduction in the cortical overlap between D3-D4 (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 23.379, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) and a significant increase in the overlap of D4-D5 (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 13.384, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) in the glued condition compared with both control sessions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of fMRI data, also shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There was a significant increase in the overlap of D4-D5 in the glued condition compared with both control sessions (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 13.384, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05).
source: This was driven by a significant reduction in the cortical overlap between D3-D4 (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 23.379, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) and a significant increase in the overlap of D4-D5 (Simple main effect: F(2,16) = 13.384, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) in the glued condition compared with both control sessions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of fMRI data, also shown in Figure 1B.

claim: No significant change was found in the overlap between D2 and D3, the glued digits, where changes have been observed in similar but longer term studies in non-human primates.
source: No significant change was found in the overlap between D2 and D3, the glued digits, where changes have been observed in similar but longer term studies in non-human primates (Clark et al., 1988; Allard et al., 1991).
evidence: This is a finding from the fMRI data analysis, contrasted with previous primate studies cited.

claim: No shift in peak-to-peak distance between the digit representations was observed.
source: No shift in peak-to-peak distance between the digit representations (Supplementary file 1) or the overall surface area of each digit representation was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the fMRI data analysis, with reference to supplementary data.

claim: No change in the overall surface area of each digit representation was observed.
source: No shift in peak-to-peak distance between the digit representations (Supplementary file 1) or the overall surface area of each digit representation was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the fMRI data analysis, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: No systematic difference in the fit between the phase-encoding models and fMRI signal were observed across sessions.
source: No systematic difference in the fit between the phase-encoding models and fMRI signal were observed across sessions (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quality control finding from the fMRI data analysis.

claim: The observed changes in cortical overlap were driven by an expansion in the representation of digit 4 adjacent to digit 5 and a corresponding contraction at the boundary with digit 3.
source: This data revealed that the observed changes presented in Figure 1B were driven by an expansion in the representation of digit 4 adjacent to digit 5 and a corresponding contraction at the boundary with digit 3.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the visualization of digit 4 representations shown in Figure 2.

claim: Data displayed for all nine participants showed a consistent shift in the representation of digit 4 at the level of individual participants, such that while there is a minimal change in peak activation and area of the representation, the flank adjacent to the representation of digit 5 expands, and the flank adjacent to digit 3 contracts.
source: These results demonstrated a consistent shift in the representation of digit 4 at the level of individual participants, such that while there is a minimal change in peak activation and area of the representation, the flank adjacent to the representation of digit 5 expands, and the flank adjacent to digit 3 contracts, consistent with the observed changes in cortical overlap (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the visualization of individual participant data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Representational similarity analysis conducted on the block design fMRI data implicated changes in the representation of digit 4.
source: Representational similarity analysis conducted on the block design fMRI data also implicated changes in the representation of digit 4 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the representational similarity analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The representational similarity analysis demonstrated a shift in the representation of D4 away from D3 and towards D5.
source: These data demonstrated a shift in the representation of D4 away from D3 and towards D5.
evidence: This is a finding from the representational similarity analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on the amount of cortical overlap (F(2.0,16.2) = 4.430, p=0.029, η2:0.356), driven by a shift in the representation of digit 4 away from digit 3 (Simple Main Effect: F(2,16) = 16.076; pairwise comparisons glued vs. control 1 and control 2: p<0.01).
source: Two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on the amount of cortical overlap (F(2.0,16.2) = 4.430, p=0.029, η2:0. 356), driven by a shift in the representation of digit 4 away from digit 3 (Simple Main Effect: F(2,16) = 16.076; pairwise comparisons glued vs. control 1 and control 2: p<0.01).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the representational similarity analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The same experimental design and gluing manipulation were applied in a separate cohort for behavioral testing.
source: Given the fMRI data were strongly suggestive of changes in cortical overlap outside of the glued digit pair (D2-D3), we sought to more fully investigate the observed pattern of short-term reorganisation by assessing the behavioural correlates of the gluing manipulation. The same experimental design and gluing manipulation were applied in a separate cohort.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for the behavioral study.

claim: Nine participants undertook behavioural psychophysics tasks during each session instead of an fMRI scan.
source: Instead of an fMRI scan, nine participants undertook behavioural psychophysics tasks during each session.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for the behavioral study.

claim: The first behavioral task involved temporal order judgment (TOJ), where pairs of rapid vibrotactile stimuli were applied to adjacent digit pairs of the right hand at varying interstimulus intervals.
source: The first task involved temporal order judgment (TOJ), where pairs of rapid vibrotactile stimuli were applied to adjacent digit pairs of the right hand at varying interstimulus intervals.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the temporal order judgment task.

claim: Greater values of JND are associated with poorer discrimination across an adjacent digit pair.
source: Greater values of JND are associated with poorer discrimination across an adjacent digit pair (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a definition of the JND metric used in the temporal order judgment task.

claim: A two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on tactile discrimination (JND) (F(4,28) = 14.613, p<0.0005, η2:0.676).
source: A two-way repeated measures ANOVA indicated a significant interaction between session and digit pair on tactile discrimination (JND) (F(4,28) = 14.613, p<0.0005, η2:0.676).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of behavioral data.

claim: There was a significant reduction in JND across D3-D4 in the gluing condition compared with both control sessions (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 14.631, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05).
source: This was driven by a significant reduction in JND across D3-D4 (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 14.631, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05), and a significant increase in the JND across D4-D5 (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 10.578, p=0.002; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) in the gluing condition compared with both control sessions (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of behavioral data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was a significant increase in the JND across D4-D5 in the gluing condition compared with both control sessions (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 10.578, p=0.002; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05).
source: This was driven by a significant reduction in JND across D3-D4 (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 14.631, p<0.0005; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05), and a significant increase in the JND across D4-D5 (Simple main effect: F(2,14) = 10.578, p=0.002; Pairwise Sidak-corrected p<0.05) in the gluing condition compared with both control sessions (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the analysis of behavioral data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No significant change in tactile discrimination was found for D2-D3, the glued digits.
source: No significant change in tactile discrimination was found for D2-D3, the glued digits.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of behavioral data.

claim: After the gluing manipulation, tactile discrimination was improved across D3-D4 and was diminished across D4-D5, with no change in the glued digits D2-D3.
source: In other words, after the gluing manipulation, tactile discrimination was improved across D3-D4 and was diminished across D4-D5, with no change in the glued digits D2-D3.
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral findings from the temporal order judgment task.

claim: There was an increase in the level of confusion between digits 4 and 5 after the gluing manipulation compared with the control conditions.
source: This finding was supported by similar results from a second task, assessing motor confusion, which involved rapidly cued button presses using individual digits. There was an increase in the level of confusion between digits 4 and 5 after the gluing manipulation compared with the control conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the motor confusion task, shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fMRI and psychophysics results present complementary evidence for functionally relevant reorganisation in human SI following just a 24 hr peripheral change in hand use.
source: The fMRI and psychophysics results present complementary evidence for functionally relevant reorganisation in human SI following just a 24 hr peripheral change in hand use.
evidence: This is a summary statement integrating the fMRI and behavioral findings.

claim: Previous longitudinal studies of detailed somatotopic remapping in humans using MEG or standard resolution fMRI have provided evidence for a general change in the distance between digit representations.
source: Previous longitudinal studies of detailed somatotopic remapping in humans using MEG or standard resolution fMRI have provided evidence for a general change in the distance between digit representations (Stavrinou et al., 2007; Mogilner et al., 1993), or a synchronisation in activity pattern of non-adjacent digits (Vidyasagar et al., 2014) after coupled stimulation across digits.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Previous longitudinal studies have provided evidence for a synchronisation in activity pattern of non-adjacent digits after coupled stimulation across digits.
source: Previous longitudinal studies of detailed somatotopic remapping in humans using MEG or standard resolution fMRI have provided evidence for a general change in the distance between digit representations (Stavrinou et al., 2007; Mogilner et al., 1993), or a synchronisation in activity pattern of non-adjacent digits (Vidyasagar et al., 2014) after coupled stimulation across digits.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: An intervention involving hand and arm immobilisation drove diminished tactile acuity and a corresponding reduction in BOLD activity in contralateral SI.
source: Conversely, an intervention involving hand and arm immobilisation drove diminished tactile acuity and a corresponding reduction in BOLD activity in contralateral SI (Lissek et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The results demonstrate that usage-dependent changes in the overlap of SI digit representations are associated with a corresponding change in the ability to differentiate tactile inputs to the digits.
source: Our results build on this work, demonstrating that usage-dependent changes in the overlap of SI digit representations are associated with a corresponding change in the ability to differentiate tactile inputs to the digits.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings in the context of previous literature.

claim: An increase in the cortical overlap between D4 and D5 was accompanied by a reduction in the tactile discrimination ability across these two digits.
source: Specifically, an increase in the cortical overlap between D4 and D5 was accompanied by a reduction in the tactile discrimination ability across these two digits.
evidence: This is a specific finding linking cortical and behavioral changes.

claim: A consistent feature of the findings was that cortical reorganisation and behavioural change was not observed for the glued digit pair (D2-D3).
source: A consistent feature of our findings was that cortical reorganisation and behavioural change was not observed for the glued digit pair (D2-D3).
evidence: This is a summary of a consistent pattern across the study's findings.

claim: Changes in cortical overlap, and corresponding change in behavioural performance, were observed for digit pairs other than the glued pair.
source: Instead, we saw changes in cortical overlap, and corresponding change in behavioural performance, for the other digit pairs.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: A shift of D4 away from D3 and towards D5 was observed.
source: Specifically, we saw a shift of D4 away from D3 and towards D5.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: These findings reject the hypothesis of increased tactile synchronisation driving an increase in cortical overlap.
source: These findings reject our hypothesis of increased tactile synchronisation driving an increase in cortical overlap.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings in relation to the initial hypothesis.

claim: The data support the alternative hypothesis that compensatory behaviour in other digits during the 24 hr manipulation drives off-target effects.
source: Instead, these data support the alternative hypothesis that compensatory behaviour in other digits during the 24 hr manipulation drives off-target effects.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings in relation to the alternative hypothesis.

claim: It is feasible that the observed remapping reflects compensatory behavioural changes in the pattern of hand use during the manipulation.
source: In light of the considerable dexterous abilities specific to the human hand (Young, 2003) and the short duration of the gluing manipulation, it is feasible that the observed remapping reflects compensatory behavioural changes in the pattern of hand use during the manipulation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings, supported by a citation about human hand dexterity.

claim: Rather than learning to coordinate and co-use the glued digits, participants may have adapted synergies with the non-manipulated digits.
source: Rather than learning to coordinate and co-use the glued digits, participants may have adapted synergies with the non-manipulated digits.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The increased physical separation of D3 and D4 during the gluing reduces the usually high degree of anatomical enslavement seen peripherally between these two digits.
source: In this case, the increased physical separation of D3 and D4 during the gluing reduces the usually high degree of anatomical enslavement seen peripherally between these two digits (Kim et al., 2008), freeing D4 to function even more synergistically with D5.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation about anatomical enslavement.

claim: This argument is supported by the observed pattern of increased motor confusion between digits 4 and 5 after the gluing manipulation, demonstrating potential changes in movement synergies, that may explain the somatosensory changes observed.
source: This argument is supported by the observed pattern of increased motor confusion between digits 4 and 5 after the gluing manipulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), demonstrating potential changes in movement synergies, that may explain the somatosensory changes observed.
evidence: This is an interpretation linking the motor confusion findings to the somatosensory changes.

claim: This finding complements recent observations that patterns of synergistic digit usage are strongly reflected in the generalisation of tactile learning from trained to adjacent untrained digits.
source: This finding complements recent observations that patterns of synergistic digit usage are strongly reflected in the generalisation of tactile learning from trained to adjacent untrained digits (Dempsey-Jones et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The two fMRI datasets showed independent evidence of a shift in the digit 4 representation during the gluing manipulation: away from digit 3, and towards digit 5.
source: The two fMRI datasets showed independent evidence of a shift in the digit 4 representation during the gluing manipulation: away from digit 3, and towards digit 5 (Figures 1 and 3), raising questions regarding the underlying mechanism driving this reorganisation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from two different fMRI analyses.

claim: Similar studies undertaken over a period of months in non-human primates have reported the emergence of overlapping receptive fields in response to the fusion of two adjacent digits.
source: Similar studies undertaken over a period of months in non-human primates have reported the emergence of overlapping receptive fields in response to the fusion of two adjacent digits (Clark et al., 1988; Allard et al., 1991).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous primate studies.

claim: It is possible that the observed changes in cortical activation could result from shifts in population receptive fields at the boundary of cortical digit representations.
source: Nonetheless, it is possible that the observed changes in cortical activation could result from shifts in population receptive fields at the boundary of cortical digit representations (Besle et al., 2014), or even changes in multidigit receptive fields (Thakur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The observed changes in cortical activation could result from changes in multidigit receptive fields.
source: Nonetheless, it is possible that the observed changes in cortical activation could result from shifts in population receptive fields at the boundary of cortical digit representations (Besle et al., 2014), or even changes in multidigit receptive fields (Thakur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Strong evidence suggests considerable plastic potential in subcortical structures, which is mirrored in the cortex.
source: As well as reorganisation in the cortex, strong evidence also suggests considerable plastic potential in subcortical structures, which is mirrored in the cortex (Jones, 1996; Rausell et al., 1998; Kambi et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The remapping observed in SI may result from reorganisation in lower level nuclei of the ascending somatosensory pathway.
source: The remapping observed in SI here may therefore result from reorganisation in lower level nuclei of the ascending somatosensory pathway.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: A shift in the cortical representation of digit 4, rather than an overall enlargement of the representation, distinguishes the observed pattern of cortical change from previous studies of artificial tactile co-activation, wherein a generalised cortical magnification of the manipulated digit is observed.
source: A shift in the cortical representation of digit 4 (Figure 2), rather than an overall enlargement of the representation, distinguishes the observed pattern of cortical change from previous studies of artificial tactile co-activation, wherein a generalised cortical magnification of the manipulated digit is observed (Pleger et al., 2001, 2003; Hodzic et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of previous literature, supported by citations.

claim: The cortical shift perhaps reflects how naturalistic behavioural changes in hand use are reflected in the cortex, with remapping based on functional need; in this case, leading to perceptual improvements in certain digit pairs (D3/D4), and worsening in others (D4/D5).
source: The cortical shift perhaps reflects how naturalistic behavioural changes in hand use are reflected in the cortex, with remapping based on functional need; in this case, leading to perceptual improvements in certain digit pairs (D3/D4), and worsening in others (D4/D5).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: In vivo studies in rodent barrel cortex demonstrate that a 24 hr period of altered sensory input can induce increases in synaptic density in the corresponding cortical representation.
source: In vivo studies in rodent barrel cortex demonstrate that a 24 hr period of altered sensory input can induce increases in synaptic density in the corresponding cortical representation (Knott et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Altered sensory input could unmask or potentiate pre-existing divergent or silenced connections between adjacent digit representations.
source: This could unmask or potentiate pre-existing divergent or silenced connections between adjacent digit representations (DeFelipe et al., 1986; Recanzone et al., 1992; Huntley, 1997).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Patterns of local horizontal connectivity in the cortex are established during development and moulded throughout life.
source: Patterns of local horizontal connectivity in the cortex are established during development and moulded throughout life (Sur and Rubenstein, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Homeostatic mechanisms exist to maintain balance in cortical activity.
source: Homeostatic mechanisms also exist to maintain balance in cortical activity (Turrigiano and Nelson, 2000), and to preserve the scaling and pattern of cortical topography (Sharma et al., 2000; Vanderhaeghen et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Homeostatic mechanisms exist to preserve the scaling and pattern of cortical topography.
source: Homeostatic mechanisms also exist to maintain balance in cortical activity (Turrigiano and Nelson, 2000), and to preserve the scaling and pattern of cortical topography (Sharma et al., 2000; Vanderhaeghen et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: It is plausible that the gluing manipulation results in the potentiation of excitatory horizontal connectivity between the representations of digits 4 and 5, and the concurrent weakening of connectivity between the representations of digits 3 and 4.
source: It is plausible that the gluing manipulation results in the potentiation of excitatory horizontal connectivity between the representations of digits 4 and 5, and the concurrent weakening of connectivity between the representations of digits 3 and 4.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: After 24 hr, the resulting pattern of cortical reorganisation is observed, wherein the relative positions of the representations have changed, but features of the maps firmly established in development, remain in place.
source: After 24 hr, we observe the resulting pattern of cortical reorganisation (Figures 2 and 3), wherein the relative positions of the representations have changed, but features of the maps firmly established in development, remain in place.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of developmental constraints.

claim: A comparable process of reduced inhibition prior to remapping has been reported in studies of sensory deprivation in rodent barrel cortex.
source: A comparable process of reduced inhibition prior to remapping has been reported in studies of sensory deprivation in rodent barrel cortex.
evidence: This statement introduces a comparison to previous literature.

claim: Reduced inputs after whisker clipping produce a local pattern of cortical disinhibition and broadening excitation, followed by subsequent cortical contraction of the representation.
source: Reduced inputs after whisker clipping produce a local pattern of cortical disinhibition and broadening excitation, followed by subsequent cortical contraction of the representation (Albieri et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Changes in the relative inputs across different digits may prompt a transient disinhibitory cortical milieu, and the subsequent re-establishment of modified excitatory networks within the cortex, wherein the cortical representations have shifted to reflect new usage patterns.
source: In this case, changes in the relative inputs across different digits may prompt a transient disinhibitory cortical milieu, and the subsequent re-establishment of modified excitatory networks within the cortex, wherein the cortical representations have shifted to reflect new usage patterns.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings based on previous literature.

claim: The unmasking of latent excitatory connections prior to any homeostatic increase in lateral inhibition to rebalance cortical excitability could explain the observation of more marked changes in tactile perception and representational surface area after very short and intense tactile training interventions, or rTMS protocols.
source: The unmasking of latent excitatory connections prior to any homeostatic increase in lateral inhibition to rebalance cortical excitability could explain the observation of more marked changes in tactile perception and representational surface area after very short and intense tactile training interventions, or rTMS protocols (Pleger et al., 2003; Tegenthoff et al., 2005; Ragert et al., 2008; Dinse and Tegenthoff, 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The consistent cortical changes at the flanks of the digit 4 representation in the absence of changes in the location of peak activation suggest that the latter may not be the most informative feature of rapid map reorganisation.
source: The consistent cortical changes at the flanks of the digit 4 representation (Figure 2) in the absence of changes in the location of peak activation suggest that the latter may not be the most informative feature of rapid map reorganisation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings regarding which features of cortical maps are most informative.

claim: The existence of hard-wired elements in cortical somatotopy is supported by evidence of SI constraining the extent of reorganisation within the somatosensory system: acting as a blueprint for lower level nuclei.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.
